canvas.arbitrary-annotations.acceptance: Keep explicit format-specific annotation policies; review any new payload schema and its PDF/SVG behavior before inclusion.
canvas.arbitrary-annotations.reason: Unrestricted native annotation payloads have no agreed portable public contract. Reviewed URL/destination annotations remain the supported interface.

codecs.scaled-subset.acceptance: Retain the exact documented scope and existing public/source/test anchors. The release audit must not promote a query, buffered operation or retained native stream into a stronger live-decoding contract.
codecs.scaled-subset.reason: The public capability supplies scaled-dimension and supported-subset negotiation. It does not promise arbitrary subset pixel decoding or a silent full-decode/crop fallback.

codecs.stream.acceptance: Retain the exact documented scope and existing public/source/test anchors. The release audit must not promote a query, buffered operation or retained native stream into a stronger live-decoding contract.
codecs.stream.reason: Private native stream ownership and explicitly buffered retained codecs are supported. The one-shot live image decoder is not a retained live-port codec session.

colors.float.acceptance: Preserve unpremultiplied channels, alpha, ARGB byte order, explicit out-of-range handling, and exhaustive per-channel byte roundtrips. Run tests/release-scope-pure-test.rkt on supported Racket versions; native color-space conversion and tone mapping are not inferred.
colors.float.reason: The existing color->color4f accepts packed ARGB through color->rgba; color4f->rgba plus color->argb supplies the reverse user operation. Extended RGB requires an explicit clipping policy. This is an idiomatic Racket equivalent, not two new bindings or a claim of binary32/rounding bit parity with every native edge case.

colors.hdr-transfer.acceptance: Test PQ/HLG numerical conventions and domains separately from tone mapping, display negotiation and physical HDR presentation.
colors.hdr-transfer.reason: PQ/HLG transfer representations are deferred with the HDR workstream. SDR transfer helpers and float storage do not establish HDR transfer or display behavior.

colors.xyz-ops.acceptance: Provide typed/detached XYZ concatenation and inversion, or demonstrate an existing color-matrix equivalent with executable ordering, singularity, finite-value and dimensionality tests. No color conversion is inferred merely from matrix multiplication.
colors.xyz-ops.reason: sk_colorspace_xyz_concat and sk_colorspace_xyz_invert remain unbound. Generic geometric matrices are not automatically a reviewed replacement for the color-space XYZ-D50 representation.

data.unsafe-memory.acceptance: Retain checked copied bytes and native-stream contracts; uninitialized public storage requires a separate explicit safety design.
data.unsafe-memory.reason: Raw uninitialized/no-copy SKData construction and arbitrary ownership callbacks are internal implementation concerns, not a safe public byte API.

documents.xps.acceptance: Before implementation, establish a concrete consumer and native Windows build support, then page/stream lifetime and independent XPS inspection.
documents.xps.reason: XPS is a separately prioritized output format, not part of the proposed PDF/SVG-focused core release. PDF is not classified as an XPS equivalent.

fonts.streams.acceptance: Retain the exact documented scope and existing public/source/test anchors. The release audit must not promote a query, buffered operation or retained native stream into a stronger live-decoding contract.
fonts.streams.reason: Native-stream and explicitly buffered font constructors are supported. This does not create a long-lived typeface backed by live Racket-port callbacks.

future.graphite.acceptance: Require native build/API support, recorder/context lifetime, submission/readback completion and shared consumer integration.
future.graphite.reason: Graphite is a different execution/recording model outside the frozen Ganesh m119 core release.

future.hdr-presentation.acceptance: Test presentation formats, transfer functions, display negotiation and SDR fallback; separate machine-testable metadata from real-display evidence.
future.hdr-presentation.reason: Physical HDR/wide-gamut presentation is outside this release scope. F16 buffers and extended numerical colors do not establish it.

future.variable-fonts.acceptance: Complete U1 ABI review or approved shim decision, then axis/palette discovery, clone lifetime, shaping and outline tests with known fonts.
future.variable-fonts.reason: Variable axes/palette cloning require an appropriate newer ABI or separately approved maintained shim. This is not a missing ordinary binding in the pinned comparison.

gpu.interface-variants.acceptance: Preserve the actual retained interface and its teardown, default factory behavior, explicit-standard rejection without silent fallback, public/source/test anchors and all additional native bindings. Retain desktop execution and backend-specific rejection checks; do not turn symbol presence into positive GLES/WebGL/browser rendering evidence.
gpu.interface-variants.reason: The selected GitHub baseline includes the 0.77c auto/desktop/GLES/WebGL interface selection and retained-interface extension queries. An explicit mode requires a matching supplied host and native build support. Owned EGL remains desktop; a WebGL factory may be a stub. Source availability and extension membership do not certify GLES/browser execution or extension usability.

gpu.trace.acceptance: Preserve the accepted implementation, source/public/test anchors and native declaration. Keep owner/current/ready/abandonment checks, detached bounded records, explicit truncation, callback cleanup and deferred errors, and no diagnostic flush, submit, wait or readback. Continue selected-backend native acceptance separately from this source audit.
gpu.trace.reason: The selected GitHub baseline includes the 0.77c context-local GPU memory-statistics implementation and its native binding. It reuses the bounded private collector with a distinct GPU-context scope; global cache reports and context-local reports remain different. Source support does not claim total VRAM/process memory or independently verified execution on every backend.

gpu.vulkan.acceptance: Require actual offscreen Vulkan pixels, transfers and teardown on exercised native builds before presentation/interop G2.
gpu.vulkan.reason: Vulkan backend ownership, synchronization and rendering remain an explicit backend expansion. Pinned declarations do not establish shipped build/device support.

images.adopt-texture.acceptance: Use reviewed interop descriptors/ownership and transfers; a new adoption contract needs backend-specific lifetime and producer/consumer evidence.
images.adopt-texture.reason: Arbitrary adopted textures introduce external deletion and synchronization obligations beyond the explicit GPU import/handoff API.

images.raw-storage.acceptance: Use copies or scoped owned buffers; review threading, callback rooting and release order before exposing any narrower zero-copy route.
images.raw-storage.reason: Unrestricted no-copy image storage and application release callbacks are excluded from the safe API.

managed.helpers.acceptance: Preserve equivalent public behavior through Racket ownership/dispatch where needed; do not count absence of a C# helper class as a graphics gap.
managed.helpers.reason: Managed .NET dispatch, dictionaries and platform glue are not user capabilities that must be duplicated in Racket.

pictures.streams.acceptance: Retain the exact documented scope and existing public/source/test anchors. The release audit must not promote a query, buffered operation or retained native stream into a stronger live-decoding contract.
pictures.streams.reason: Retain the accepted native stream picture contract and its trust/audit restrictions. Other picture publication entry points remain described by their own checked public anchors.

pixels.bitmap-aliasing.acceptance: Keep arbitrary pointer aliases out of the public API; any future zero-copy route must supply storage ownership, invalidation and native callback tests.
pixels.bitmap-aliasing.reason: Raw SKBitmap install/reset/alias operations bypass the owned raster-buffer and scoped pixmap lifecycle.

pixels.raw-pixmap.acceptance: Retain detached metadata and guarded pixmap views; do not add pointer access merely to close a native-symbol count.
pixels.raw-pixmap.reason: Raw pixel addresses and descriptor reset can escape the validated scoped-borrow contract.

surfaces.null.acceptance: Implement and test a safe null-surface contract, or explicitly exclude the surface factory with a reviewed rationale and documented no-draw alternative. Check zero/invalid extents, closure, borrowed canvases and snapshot limitations.
surfaces.null.reason: The pinned sk_surface_new_null declaration remains unbound. A scoped no-draw canvas already exists, but it does not establish a null surface with the same ownership, sizing, or snapshot behavior. Do not erase this gap using a canvas synonym.
